To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned and characterized the thiD/J genes encoding a bifunctional HMP kinase/phosphomethpyrimidine kinase in Escherichia coil.
thiDIJ encodes a bifunctional protein that catalyzes the conversion of HMP to its pyrophosphorylated product.
the thiDIJ locus of E. coli encodes a single polypeptide with two distinct enzymatic activities, i.e., HMP kinase and phosphomethpyrimidine kinase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and characterization of the gene encoding a thiamine-synthesizing enzyme, HMP kinase/HMP-P kinase, in Escherichia Coli.
the cloning of the thiDIJ gene of E. coli.
the cloning and expression of thiDIJ gene of E. coli, which encodes a thiamin-biosynthetic bifunctional enzyme HMP kinase/HMP-P kinase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thiDIJ gene encodes the thiamin-synthesis enzyme HMP-P kinase and HMP kinase.
the thiD gene of Escherchia coli encodes the thiamin-synthesis enzyme, HMP kinase/HMP-p kinase, and the thiJ gene encodes the thiazole-synthesis enzyme, hydroxyethylthiozole kinase.
thiD encodes HMP kinase and thiJ encodes HMP-P kinase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiamin biosynthetic pathway in Escherichia coil is composed of 11 steps catalyzed by 10 enzymes, and all the enzymes except for thiD/J are encoded by single genes.
the thiDIJ gene is responsible for the conversion of HMP to thiamin monophosphate.
the thiM gene encodes HET kinase, the thiJ gene encodes HMP kinase and thiD encodes HMP-P kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thiDIJ gene encodes a thiamin-biosynthetic enzyme that is a bifunctional protein, HMP kinase/HMP-p kinase.
the two distinct enzymes activities, HMPK and HMP-PK are indeed a bifuncional enzyme encoded by a thiDIJ gene.
the thiDIJ locus is a single gene encoding a thiamine synthesizing bifunctional protein, HMP kinase/HMP-P kinase.
